answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring every identity to lock a refundable stake before it can trade. A single honest agent pays once, but an attacker who wants a meadow of fake identities must fund each one, so the cost grows with every copy. If a fake is caught cheating, its stake is slashed and paid to its victims, turning a canyon of cheap sock-puppets into an expensive liability. Honest work earns the stake back, so the garden of real participants stays affordable while forgery becomes unprofitable.
